item.title: How Public Places Hold Memory
item.description: Follow a walk through a changing city and practise describing how buildings, routes and memorials preserve or reshape traces of the past.

children.definition: Characteristic of the traditional building practices of a particular place.
children.example: The deep eaves and shaded porches are typical of the district’s vernacular architecture.

children.definition: Allowing people to pass through easily at several points.
children.example: The market’s porous boundary lets shoppers enter from any of the three surrounding streets and walk straight through to the next block.
children.translation_ru: со свободным проходом в нескольких местах
children.translation_uz: bir necha joyidan bemalol oʻtish mumkin boʻlgan

children.definition: A place that has changed repeatedly and still bears visible traces of earlier periods.
children.example: The square is a palimpsest: stone troughs from the old livestock market stand beside rails from the later tram terminus, and both are still visible during the weekly craft market.
children.translation_ru: место, где сохранились следы разных эпох
children.translation_uz: turli davrlarning izlari saqlanib qolgan joy
collocations: read the city as a palimpsest

children.definition: The physical separation of places by a barrier that makes movement between them difficult.
children.example: The ring road created spatial severance between the housing estate and the riverside park.
children.translation_uz: jismoniy toʻsiq tufayli hududlarning ajralishi va ular orasida qatnovning qiyinlashishi

children.definition: The gradual growth of something as small additions build up over time.
children.example: The courtyard took shape through the gradual accretion of sheds, lean-tos and covered walkways.
children.translation_ru: постепенное нарастание за счёт небольших добавлений
children.translation_uz: mayda qismlar qoʻshila borishi natijasida biror narsaning asta-sekin kattalashishi

children.definition: A memorial designed to challenge conventional ways of commemorating the past.
children.example: The artist’s counter-monument invites visitors to write the names of displaced families in chalk and let the rain wash them away.
children.translation_ru: мемориал, ставящий под сомнение привычные способы сохранения памяти о прошлом
children.translation_uz: oʻtmishni yodga olishning odatiy usullarini qayta koʻrib chiqishga undash uchun yaratilgan yodgorlik

children.definition: The pattern formed by the size and arrangement of streets, blocks and plots in a built-up area.
children.example: The library respects the fine urban grain of the old quarter: its three wings follow the boundaries of the original narrow plots, and the alley between two of them remains open.
children.translation_ru: структура городской ткани, определяемая размерами и расположением улиц, кварталов и участков
children.translation_uz: koʻchalar, ular bilan chegaralangan kvartallar va yer uchastkalarining oʻlchami hamda joylashuvi belgilaydigan shahar tuzilishi

children.definition: The practice of adapting an existing building to serve a different purpose.
children.example: The conversion of the old baths into rehearsal rooms is an example of adaptive reuse that preserves the tiled entrance hall.
children.translation_ru: приспособление существующего здания для нового назначения

children.definition: An informal path worn by people repeatedly taking a route of their own choosing.
children.example: A desire line cuts across the lawn where commuters head straight for the station steps.
children.translation_ru: тропа, протоптанная пешеходами по удобному для них маршруту
children.translation_uz: piyodalar oʻzlariga qulay yoʻldan qatnab hosil qilgan soʻqmoq

children.definition: A small surviving trace of something that has largely disappeared.
children.example: A row of iron rings set into the paving is the last vestige of the cattle market.

children.definition: To erase a visible mark or trace so that it can no longer be seen.
children.example: Resurfacing the lane would efface the wheel ruts left by carts that once served the warehouses.

children.definition: Construction on vacant or underused land within an already built-up area.
children.example: A row of infill housing now occupies the gap between the school and the corner shops.
children.translation_ru: строительство на свободных или малоиспользуемых участках среди существующих зданий
children.translation_uz: binolar qurilgan hudud ichidagi boʻsh yoki kam foydalanilayotgan yer uchastkalariga bino qurish

children.definition: To put words or other marks on a surface, often by cutting them into it.
children.example: Volunteers asked a stonecarver to inscribe the names of former stallholders on the fountain’s rim.
children.translation_ru: наносить на поверхность надпись или знак, часто вырезая их
children.translation_uz: sirtga yozuv yoki belgi tushirmoq, koʻpincha uni oʻyib yozmoq yoki chizmoq

children.definition: To force people to leave the place where they live.
children.example: When the flats above the arcade were converted into holiday lets, the change displaced several long-term tenants.
children.translation_uz: odamlarni oʻz uylarini tark etishga majbur qilmoq
